metadata.case_name: WONG TING HONG v. LI HON CHUEN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: third-year student in a Bachelor of Arts course in Social Science at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
plaintiff.occupation_after: full-time teaching assistant in the Sociology Department of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (since 1st August 1988)
plaintiff.education_level: Bachelor of Arts (completed Master degree in Sociology in 1988)

injuries.description: Fracture of the left femur (treated with traction and insertion of an intramedullary nail).
source: The leg was put on traction and on 3rd November 1983 an open intramedullary nail was inserted into the left femur.

injuries.description: Scars: a 2" scar on the buttock and a 4" scar on the left thigh.
source: apart from a 2" scar on the buttock and a 4" scar on the left thigh he was left with no permanent impairments according to the medical reports.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple superficial injuries of hip or thigh

manifestations.description: Pain and inconvenience for a considerable time prior to the removal of the nail
Discomfort and soreness in particular when the weather changes
Not able to run as fast and be so proficient as a forward at football (previously enjoyed football, basketball and volleyball)
Unable to continue his study in the academic year of 1983-1984 and had to repeat his third year in 1984-1985

treatments_received: open intramedullary nailing of the left femur (3rd November 1983)
removal of the intramedullary nail (three days hospitalisation in August 1985)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Not able to run as fast and be so proficient as a forward at football which he particularly enjoyed before the accident.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Unable to continue his study in the academic year of 1983-1984 and had to repeat his third year in 1984-1985 (education deferred for one academic year).
Permanent scarring: a 2" scar on the buttock and a 4" scar on the left thigh.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Yuk-seung v. Lee Tat-shu and another
comparable_cases.injury_description: fractures to the right femur, patella and talus. The Plaintiff was hospitalised for almost three months and had two further operations when plates were inserted. He suffered a permanent weakness of the right leg and risk of injury to the exposed knee joint.
compound fracture of the right humerus, and a fracture of the right tibia and fibula. He suffered no permanent disability apart from sporadic spells of dizziness.
